title: The retrograde post-shadow, and why you don't feel better yet | Ask Tota
description: The retrograde ends and nothing resolves. That is because Mercury is crossing the same degrees a third time. Here is what the shadow periods are and what they aren't.
og_title: The post-shadow, and why u don't feel better yet
og_description: Mercury stations direct and everyone expects a reset. It doesn't come, because the same stretch of sky is still being walked over.
h1: the retrograde ended. why does nothing feel finished?
dek: mercury stations direct on 13 november and the internet declares it over. it isn't, because the same fifteen degrees are still being crossed for a third time. here is what a shadow period actually is, and how much of it to believe.

faq.a: the stretch after a planet stations direct, while it re-crosses the degrees it had already covered during the retrograde. it ends when the planet finally passes the degree where it originally stationed retrograde.

faq.q: when does the 2026 mercury post-shadow end?
faq.a: around 30 november. mercury stations direct on 13 november and then takes a further two to three weeks to clear the degrees it had already walked over.

faq.q: why is it called a shadow?
faq.a: because the planet passes through the same slice of zodiac three times: forwards, backwards, then forwards again. that thrice-crossed slice is the shadow, and it is the same degrees on all three passes.
the mirror image at the front. it starts when the planet first crosses the degree it will later retrograde back to, and runs until the retrograde station.

faq.q: is the shadow period a classical vedic idea?
faq.a: no. the shadow framing is modern, and it comes out of western astrological practice. the classical vedic vocabulary has vakri for retrograde and atichari for fast motion, and does not build a three-phase model around it.

faq.q: so why do people still feel unsettled after it ends?
faq.a: mostly because three weeks of deferred admin does not clear itself in a day. things reopened during the window take time to close, and that is ordinary scheduling rather than sky mechanics.

faq.q: how long is the whole cycle including shadows?
faq.a: roughly nine to ten weeks per retrograde. three of retrograde, and about three either side. across three windows a year that is a large fraction of the calendar, which is worth noticing before treating it as a caution.

faq.q: should i wait until the post-shadow ends to make decisions?
faq.a: if u count shadows, u are cautioning about a third of every year. no working tradition ever asked people to defer a third of their lives, and following it would cost u far more than any transit ever has.

faq.q: does the direct station feel like anything?
faq.a: the station is the part practitioners weight most, because the planet sits on one degree for days instead of sprinting through a sign. whether u notice it is a separate question and one there is no evidence for.

faq.q: what is a good use for the post-shadow window?
faq.a: closing loops. finish the thing u reopened, send the follow-up, sign what u deferred. that is a scheduling habit, and it works whether or not the astrology does.

faq.q: do other planets have shadow periods?
faq.a: the same geometry applies to every retrograding planet, so yes. nobody tracks saturn's shadow, even though saturn is retrograde for more of the year than mercury.

faq.q: how do i know which degrees the shadow covers?
faq.a: note the degree where the planet stations retrograde and the degree where it stations direct. everything between those two points is the shadow, and it gets crossed three times.
